title: Miles Davis's original trumpet sound after Armstrong
summary: Gil argues Miles created the first new trumpet sound since Armstrong through hard work, and compares Coltrane and Billie Holiday.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: I mean Miles Davis still has to work, I mean he worked hard. I mean he has to exert the most tremendous control to play the way he does. Aside from blowing power, the strength of embouchure, everything. When he works it's real labor.

I mean, somebody coming up, born afterwards, being raised on his sound just automatically plays it and does it because it's there. But he had to create it. He had to create it against all ( ? and that he didn't like?). But he couldn't play and sound like anybody else, it didn't want to sound like anybody else because he couldn't, he couldn't be, I don't know, he couldn't be a musician and sound like anybody else. He didn't know that. That developed. And you go along, you try and you start out, you sound like so and so. Various
players like Clark Terry and Freddy Webster ( ? ), and other ones that I don't know. The early ones I'm Los Angeles and all that?). Harry James was an early one.

But eventually had run all those wave forms together and come out with his own original wave form because nobody else ever had that sound before. That's the first complete new sound on the trumpet that goes since Louis Armstrong.

Everybody up until Miles Davis played an extension of Louis Armstrong. Even though it may have been camouflaged (categorized?) by high style and all that, it was still the basic sound, it was still based on Louis Armstrong and Miles Davis changed the sound. And that's a hard job that he did. It took a lot of work. It took a lot of hard work for him to keep doing it.

And other people came along and just do it because it's a household sound. You know, you can get it, you can get jazz and do it. I've seen, happens with Coltrane, did the same thing. It's a definite original wave form. Billie Holiday had that.
Everybody doesn't have that. But you can become a great artist without creating your own individual characteristic tone or a wave form. You can still

become a great artists by style, musicality, musicianship and taste and all those things count. There are lots of great artists that don't have their own original tone. They use another tone, somebody elses tone to work on and to work their style into. But it isn't the basic, basic tone change.
And that's something that one does what, hear in your head?
Hear in your head. You hear it in your head and it has to finally come out. You've got to get it or you can't go on if you can't get it. So you have to get it.
And then of course, with someone like you, you have to get it with a whole orchestra?

Get it with the combination of instruments. I have to make those instruments combine to get a sound like no other instrument could get by itself. It's a new sound made by a combination of instruments is what I have to do in order to get it, to get an orchestra sound. That's what I have to do before my Monday night. (concerts).
